To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the donor-stabilized "half-parent" zwitterionic phosphasilene 7 is capable of transferring its parent phosphinideno moiety to unsaturated organic substrates.

the zwitterionic "parent" phosphasilene can be stabilized by coordination of two DMAP ligands to the Si center and that this stabilized zwitterionic "phosphasilene" 8 can transfer the elusive "phosphinidene" moiety (:PH).

the zwitterionic half-parent phosphasilene 1,1-dimethyl-2-(dimethylaminomethylideneamino)-1-sila-2-phosphanediene 4 is capable of transferring a parent phosphinidyl moiety (:PH), and that it is capable of adding small molecules like dimethylzinc or ammonia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and reactivity of a donor-stabilized phosphasilene 1,2-oxazaphosphasilinane, and its reactivity towards small organic molecules.

the synthesis of a novel donor-stabilized "half-parent" zwitterionic phosphasilene, which is capable of transferring its parent phosphinidyl moiety and of reacting with small molecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the zwitterionic "parent" phosphasilene is not stable enough to be observed, but that it can be stabilized by coordination to a donor ligand.
the Si=P bond in 4 and 4-donor-stabilized zirconium complexes 7 and 8 are capable of adding to small molecules, such as H2S, NH3 and organoamines.
compounds 4 and its adduct 8 are not stable phosphasilenes at all, but rather zwitterionic "parent"-type compounds that are capable of undergoing a variety of unusual reactions with small molecules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Si=P bond of 4 and 4-donor-stabilized zirconium phosphasilenes can act as a Lewis acid and a Lewis base at the same time.
compounds 4 and, in particular, 8 are capable of reacting with a wide variety of substrates, including small molecules, affording a variety of new compounds, some of which are unprecedented.

the Si=P bond of the zwitterionic "parent" phosphasilenes 4 and 4-donor is capable of activating small molecules such as H2S and HNHR, which is in analogy to the reactivity of the "free" parent phosphasilene 1.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the zwitterionic "parent" phosphasilene L'Si=PR (R=H, L=HC(CMe2[2,6- iPr2C6 H3N])2) is stabilized by the addition of a donor-stabilized, bulky, and electron-rich phosphanyl group (L'Si-PH2), which is capable of transferring a :PH fragment to unsaturated substrates.
the zwitterionic "free" phosphanylphosphinidene (:PH-PH2) is a viable reactive intermediate, which may be stabilized by coordination with a donor ligand.
the phosphasilene 2,4,6-triisopropylbenzylphosphasilene 4 can act as a "half-parent" of the elusive parent phosphasilene, if stabilized by a donor ligand.
